meaning:
ἐπι-βαρέω, -ῶ
to put a burden on, be burdensome: figuratively, absol., 2Co.2:6; with accusative of person(s), 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8 (cf. M, Th., I, 29).†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: we would not be a burden
we would not be a burden

elsewhere.note: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow, not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.
For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail; for working night and day, that we might not burden any of you, we preached to you the Good News of God.
neither did we eat bread from anyone’s hand without paying for it, but in labor and travail worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you,
